pattern.title: Problems on Ages
pattern.description: Age equations and ratios across time.

questions.questionText: The sum of the present ages of a mother and his daughter is 59 years and the mother is 49 years older than the daughter. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation: Older + younger = 59, older - younger = 49. Older = (59 + 49)/2 = 54 years.
questions.shortcut: Older = (sum + difference)/2; younger = (sum - difference)/2.

questions.questionText: The sum of the present ages of a mother and his daughter is 84 years and the mother is 34 years older than the daughter. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation: Older + younger = 84, older - younger = 34. Older = (84 + 34)/2 = 59 years.
questions.shortcut: Older = (sum + difference)/2; younger = (sum - difference)/2.

questions.questionText: The sum of the present ages of a uncle and his nephew is 55 years and the uncle is 33 years older than the nephew. What is the uncle's present age?
questions.explanation: Older + younger = 55, older - younger = 33. Older = (55 + 33)/2 = 44 years.
questions.shortcut: Older = (sum + difference)/2; younger = (sum - difference)/2.

questions.questionText: The sum of the present ages of a teacher and his student is 53 years and the teacher is 21 years older than the student. What is the teacher's present age?
questions.explanation: Older + younger = 53, older - younger = 21. Older = (53 + 21)/2 = 37 years.
questions.shortcut: Older = (sum + difference)/2; younger = (sum - difference)/2.

questions.questionText: A father is 5 times as old as his son. If the sum of their ages is 66 years, what is the son's age?
questions.explanation: Let the son's age be x. Then x + 5x = 66, so 6x = 66 and x = 11 years.
questions.shortcut: The ages are in the ratio 1:5; divide the sum into 6 parts.

questions.questionText: A teacher is 2 times as old as his student. If the sum of their ages is 45 years, what is the student's age?
questions.explanation: Let the student's age be x. Then x + 2x = 45, so 3x = 45 and x = 15 years.
questions.shortcut: The ages are in the ratio 1:2; divide the sum into 3 parts.

questions.questionText: A mother is 4 times as old as his daughter. If the sum of their ages is 55 years, what is the daughter's age?
questions.explanation: Let the daughter's age be x. Then x + 4x = 55, so 5x = 55 and x = 11 years.
questions.shortcut: The ages are in the ratio 1:4; divide the sum into 5 parts.

questions.questionText: A uncle is 2 times as old as his nephew. If the sum of their ages is 18 years, what is the nephew's age?
questions.explanation: Let the nephew's age be x. Then x + 2x = 18, so 3x = 18 and x = 6 years.
questions.shortcut: The ages are in the ratio 1:2; divide the sum into 3 parts.

questions.questionText: A teacher is 3 times as old as his student. If the sum of their ages is 36 years, what is the student's age?
questions.explanation: Let the student's age be x. Then x + 3x = 36, so 4x = 36 and x = 9 years.
questions.shortcut: The ages are in the ratio 1:3; divide the sum into 4 parts.

questions.questionText: A mother is 4 times as old as his daughter. If the sum of their ages is 75 years, what is the daughter's age?
questions.explanation: Let the daughter's age be x. Then x + 4x = 75, so 5x = 75 and x = 15 years.
questions.shortcut: The ages are in the ratio 1:4; divide the sum into 5 parts.

questions.questionText: A uncle is 3 times as old as his nephew. The difference between their ages is 16 years. What is the uncle's age?
questions.explanation: Let the nephew's age be x: 3x - x = 16, so x = 8. The uncle is 3 x 8 = 24 years old.
questions.shortcut: Difference = (3 - 1) parts, so one part = 16/2.

questions.questionText: A mother is 6 times as old as his daughter. The difference between their ages is 65 years. What is the mother's age?
questions.explanation: Let the daughter's age be x: 6x - x = 65, so x = 13. The mother is 6 x 13 = 78 years old.
questions.shortcut: Difference = (6 - 1) parts, so one part = 65/5.

questions.questionText: The ages of a teacher and his student are in the ratio 9:4 and the difference between their ages is 25 years. What is the teacher's age?
questions.explanation: Difference = (9 - 4) parts = 25, so one part = 5. Teacher = 9 x 5 = 45 years.
questions.shortcut: Difference of the ratio terms corresponds to the age gap.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the present ages of a uncle and his nephew is 3:2 and the sum of their ages is 15 years. What is the uncle's age?
questions.explanation: Parts = 3 + 2 = 5. One part = 15/5 = 3. Uncle = 3 x 3 = 9 years.
questions.shortcut: Divide the sum in the given ratio.

questions.questionText: The ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 9:4 and the difference between their ages is 35 years. What is the father's age?
questions.explanation: Difference = (9 - 4) parts = 35, so one part = 7. Father = 9 x 7 = 63 years.
questions.shortcut: Difference of the ratio terms corresponds to the age gap.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the present ages of a father and his son is 3:2 and the sum of their ages is 30 years. What is the father's age?
questions.explanation: Parts = 3 + 2 = 5. One part = 30/5 = 6. Father = 3 x 6 = 18 years.
questions.shortcut: Divide the sum in the given ratio.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the present ages of a father and his son is 5:2 and the sum of their ages is 49 years. What is the father's age?
questions.explanation: Parts = 5 + 2 = 7. One part = 49/7 = 7. Father = 5 x 7 = 35 years.
questions.shortcut: Divide the sum in the given ratio.

questions.questionText: The ages of a uncle and his nephew are in the ratio 4:1 and the difference between their ages is 15 years. What is the uncle's age?
questions.explanation: Difference = (4 - 1) parts = 15, so one part = 5. Uncle = 4 x 5 = 20 years.
questions.shortcut: Difference of the ratio terms corresponds to the age gap.

questions.questionText: The ratio of the present ages of a uncle and his nephew is 3:2 and the sum of their ages is 25 years. What is the uncle's age?
questions.explanation: Parts = 3 + 2 = 5. One part = 25/5 = 5. Uncle = 3 x 5 = 15 years.
questions.shortcut: Divide the sum in the given ratio.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a uncle and his nephew are in the ratio 8:5. After 10 years the ratio will be 22:15. What is the uncle's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 8k and 5k. (8k + 10)/(5k + 10) = 22/15. Cross-multiplying: k(120 - 110) = 10(22 - 15), so k = 7 and the uncle is 8 x 7 = 56 years old.
questions.shortcut: Put the ages as ak and bk, apply the change, cross-multiply and solve for k.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a mother and his daughter are in the ratio 5:2. After 3 years the ratio will be 23:11. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 5k and 2k. (5k + 3)/(2k + 3) = 23/11. Cross-multiplying: k(55 - 46) = 3(23 - 11), so k = 4 and the mother is 5 x 4 = 20 years old.
questions.shortcut: Put the ages as ak and bk, apply the change, cross-multiply and solve for k.

questions.questionText: The ages of a uncle and his nephew are in the ratio 3:1. If the uncle is 18 years older than the nephew, how old will the nephew be after 5 years?
questions.explanation: One part = 18/(3 - 1) = 9. Nephew now = 1 x 9 = 9. After 5 years = 14 years.
questions.shortcut: Find the present age first, then add the years.

questions.questionText: The ages of a teacher and his student are in the ratio 5:2. If the teacher is 33 years older than the student, how old will the student be after 5 years?
questions.explanation: One part = 33/(5 - 2) = 11. Student now = 2 x 11 = 22. After 5 years = 27 years.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a mother and his daughter are in the ratio 7:5. After 8 years the ratio will be 29:23. What is the mother's present age?

questions.shortcut: Put the ages as ak and bk, apply the change, cross-multiply and solve for k.

questions.questionText: The ages of a mother and his daughter are in the ratio 9:4. If the mother is 40 years older than the daughter, how old will the daughter be after 5 years?

questions.questionText: The ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 7:2. If the father is 45 years older than the son, how old will the son be after 5 years?

questions.explanation: Let the ages be 3k and 2k. (3k + 8)/(2k + 8) = 17/14. Cross-multiplying: k(42 - 34) = 8(17 - 14), so k = 3 and the mother is 3 x 3 = 9 years old.

questions.questionText: The ages of a uncle and his nephew are in the ratio 7:3. If the uncle is 24 years older than the nephew, how old will the nephew be after 5 years?

questions.questionText: The present ages of a mother and his daughter are in the ratio 4:3. After 5 years the ratio will be 21:17. What is the mother's present age?

questions.shortcut: Put the ages as ak and bk, apply the change, cross-multiply and solve for k.

questions.questionText: The ages of a mother and his daughter are in the ratio 7:2. If the mother is 55 years older than the daughter, how old will the daughter be after 5 years?
questions.explanation: One part = 55/(7 - 2) = 11. Daughter now = 2 x 11 = 22. After 5 years = 27 years.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a teacher and his student are in the ratio 5:3. 2 years ago the ratio was 19:11. What is the student's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 5k and 3k. (5k - 2)/(3k - 2) = 19/11. Cross-multiplying gives k(55 - 57) = 2(11 - 19), so k = 8. The student is 3 x 8 = 24 years old.
questions.shortcut: Same method as the future case, but subtract the years.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 5:2. After 10 years the ratio will be 5:3. What is the difference between their ages?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 5k and 2k. (5k + 10)/(2k + 10) = 5/3 gives k = 4. Difference = (5 - 2) x 4 = 12 years.
questions.shortcut: The age gap never changes: it is (a - b) x k.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a mother and his daughter are in the ratio 3:2. After 6 years the ratio will be 21:16. What is the difference between their ages?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 3k and 2k. (3k + 6)/(2k + 6) = 21/16 gives k = 5. Difference = (3 - 2) x 5 = 5 years.
questions.shortcut: The age gap never changes: it is (a - b) x k.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a father and his son are in the ratio 8:5. 4 years ago the ratio was 5:3. What is the son's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 8k and 5k. (8k - 4)/(5k - 4) = 5/3. Cross-multiplying gives k(24 - 25) = 4(3 - 5), so k = 8. The son is 5 x 8 = 40 years old.
questions.shortcut: Same method as the future case, but subtract the years.

questions.questionText: The present ages of a teacher and his student are in the ratio 3:2. 2 years ago the ratio was 19:12. What is the student's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the ages be 3k and 2k. (3k - 2)/(2k - 2) = 19/12. Cross-multiplying gives k(36 - 38) = 2(12 - 19), so k = 7. The student is 2 x 7 = 14 years old.
questions.shortcut: Same method as the future case, but subtract the years.

questions.questionText: A uncle is 31 years old and his nephew is 12 years old. In how many years will the uncle be twice as old as the nephew?
questions.explanation: After t years: 31 + t = 2(12 + t), so t = 31 - 24 = 7 years.
questions.shortcut: Set up (older + t) = k x (younger + t) and solve.

questions.questionText: 5 years ago a uncle was 4 times as old as his nephew. If the nephew is 16 years old now, what is the uncle's present age?
questions.explanation: Nephew's age 5 years ago = 11. The uncle then = 4 x 11 = 44. Now = 44 + 5 = 49 years.
questions.shortcut: Work in the past, then add the years back to get present age.

questions.questionText: A uncle is 44 years old and his nephew is 16 years old. In how many years will the uncle be twice as old as the nephew?
questions.explanation: After t years: 44 + t = 2(16 + t), so t = 44 - 32 = 12 years.
questions.shortcut: Set up (older + t) = k x (younger + t) and solve.

questions.questionText: 6 years ago a uncle was 2 times as old as his nephew. If the nephew is 17 years old now, what is the uncle's present age?

questions.questionText: 6 years ago a teacher was 5 times as old as his student. If the student is 22 years old now, what is the teacher's present age?

questions.questionText: A father is 26 years old and his son is 16 years old. How many years ago was the father exactly 3 times as old as the son?

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of a uncle and his nephew will be 60 years after 4 years. If the uncle is 24 years older than the nephew, what is the uncle's present age?
questions.explanation: Present sum = 60 - 2 x 4 = 52. Older = (52 + 24)/2 = 38 years.
questions.shortcut: Each person ages by t, so subtract 2t from the future sum to get today's sum.

questions.questionText: A teacher's age is 5 times his student's age. After 12 years the teacher will be 3 times as old as the student. What is the teacher's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the student be x: 5x + 12 = 3(x + 12), so 2x = 24 and x = 12. The teacher is 5 x 12 = 60 years old.
questions.shortcut: Express both ages with x and equate after the shift.

questions.questionText: A father's age is 5 times his son's age. After 6 years the father will be 4 times as old as the son. What is the father's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the son be x: 5x + 6 = 4(x + 6), so 1x = 18 and x = 18. The father is 5 x 18 = 90 years old.
questions.shortcut: Express both ages with x and equate after the shift.

questions.questionText: 4 years ago a mother was 7 times as old as his daughter. After 4 years, he will be 3 times as old as the daughter. What is the mother's present age?
questions.explanation: Let daughter = x now, mother = f. f - 4 = 7(x - 4) and f + 4 = 3(x + 4). Subtracting: 8 = 3(x + 4) - 7(x - 4), which gives x = 8 and f = 32 years.
questions.shortcut: Write both conditions as equations in the two present ages and solve.

questions.questionText: 5 years ago a uncle was 3 times as old as his nephew. After 5 years, he will be 2 times as old as the nephew. What is the uncle's present age?
questions.explanation: Let nephew = x now, uncle = f. f - 5 = 3(x - 5) and f + 5 = 2(x + 5). Subtracting: 10 = 2(x + 5) - 3(x - 5), which gives x = 15 and f = 35 years.
questions.shortcut: Write both conditions as equations in the two present ages and solve.

questions.questionText: A uncle's age is 3 times his nephew's age. After 10 years the uncle will be 2 times as old as the nephew. What is the uncle's present age?
questions.explanation: Let the nephew be x: 3x + 10 = 2(x + 10), so 1x = 10 and x = 10. The uncle is 3 x 10 = 30 years old.

questions.questionText: A teacher is 21 years old and his student is 5 years old. What will be the sum of their ages after 15 years?

questions.questionText: A father is 2 times as old as his son who is 15 years old. How old will the father be when the son is 21 years old?

questions.questionText: The sum of the present ages of a teacher and his student is 90 years. 6 years ago the teacher was 69 years old. How old is the student today?
questions.explanation: The teacher is 69 + 6 = 75 years old today. Student = 90 - 75 = 15 years.

questions.questionText: The sum of the present ages of a teacher and his student is 84 years. 4 years ago the teacher was 66 years old. How old is the student today?

questions.questionText: 5 children were born at intervals of 2 years each. If the youngest is 4 years old, how old is the eldest?
questions.explanation: There are 4 gaps of 2 years between the youngest and the eldest. Eldest = 4 + 4 x 2 = 12 years.
questions.shortcut: Eldest = youngest + (number of children - 1) x interval.

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of 6 children born at intervals of 3 years each is 93 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
questions.explanation: The ages are y, y + 3, y + 6 and so on up to y + 15. Sum = 6y + 3 x 15 = 93, so y = 8 years.
questions.shortcut: Average of the ages is the middle value; step back by half the span.

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of 3 children born at intervals of 4 years each is 30 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
questions.explanation: The ages are y, y + 4, y + 8 and so on up to y + 8. Sum = 3y + 4 x 3 = 30, so y = 6 years.
questions.shortcut: Average of the ages is the middle value; step back by half the span.

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of 3 children born at intervals of 3 years each is 30 years. What is the age of the youngest child?
questions.explanation: The ages are y, y + 3, y + 6 and so on up to y + 6. Sum = 3y + 3 x 3 = 30, so y = 7 years.
questions.shortcut: Average of the ages is the middle value; step back by half the span.

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of 3 children born at intervals of 2 years each is 30 years. In how many years will the sum of their ages be 42 years?
questions.explanation: Every child gains 1 year per year, so the sum rises by 3 per year. Years = (42 - 30)/3 = 4.
questions.shortcut: Sum of ages grows by (number of people) every year.

questions.questionText: The sum of the ages of 4 children born at intervals of 4 years each is 68 years. In how many years will the sum of their ages be 92 years?
questions.explanation: Every child gains 1 year per year, so the sum rises by 4 per year. Years = (92 - 68)/4 = 6.
questions.shortcut: Sum of ages grows by (number of people) every year.

questions.questionText: Bala is 4 years older than Divya, and Divya is 2 times as old as Anil. The sum of their ages is 34 years. How old is Anil?
questions.explanation: Let Anil = x, Divya = 2x, Bala = 2x + 4. Sum = 5x + 4 = 34, so x = 6 years.
questions.shortcut: Express every age in terms of the youngest person.

questions.questionText: Divya is 4 years older than Anil, and Anil is 3 times as old as Farid. The sum of their ages is 102 years. How old is Farid?
questions.explanation: Let Farid = x, Anil = 3x, Divya = 3x + 4. Sum = 7x + 4 = 102, so x = 14 years.
questions.shortcut: Express every age in terms of the youngest person.

questions.questionText: Divya is 3 years older than Farid, and Farid is 3 times as old as Charan. The sum of their ages is 45 years. How old is Charan?
questions.explanation: Let Charan = x, Farid = 3x, Divya = 3x + 3. Sum = 7x + 3 = 45, so x = 6 years.

questions.questionText: Anil is 5 years older than Charan, who is 3 years older than Bala. If the sum of the ages of all three is 50 years, what is Anil's age?
questions.explanation: Let Bala = x, Charan = x + 3, Anil = x + 8. Sum = 3x + 11 = 50, so x = 13 and Anil = 21 years.
questions.shortcut: Take the youngest as x and add the gaps.

questions.questionText: Charan is 5 years older than Farid, who is 2 years older than Esha. If the sum of the ages of all three is 45 years, what is Charan's age?
questions.explanation: Let Esha = x, Farid = x + 2, Charan = x + 7. Sum = 3x + 9 = 45, so x = 12 and Charan = 19 years.

questions.questionText: Divya is 7 years older than Bala, who is 5 years older than Farid. If the sum of the ages of all three is 44 years, what is Divya's age?

questions.questionText: Farid is 6 years older than Charan, who is 2 years older than Esha. If the sum of the ages of all three is 46 years, what is Farid's age?

questions.questionText: Bala is 5 years older than Anil, who is 2 years older than Esha. If the sum of the ages of all three is 54 years, what is Bala's age?

questions.questionText: The ages of Anil and Farid are in the ratio 3:5, and the ages of Farid and Divya are in the ratio 2:3. If the sum of all three ages is 62 years, what is Divya's age?
questions.explanation: Make Farid's part equal: Anil:Farid:Divya = 6:10:15. Sum of parts = 31, so one part = 62/31 = 2. Divya = 15 x 2 = 30 years.
questions.shortcut: Combine the two ratios into A:B:C first, then split the total.

questions.questionText: The ages of Anil and Bala are in the ratio 3:5, and the ages of Bala and Esha are in the ratio 3:5. If the sum of all three ages is 98 years, what is Esha's age?
questions.explanation: Make Bala's part equal: Anil:Bala:Esha = 9:15:25. Sum of parts = 49, so one part = 98/49 = 2. Esha = 25 x 2 = 50 years.
questions.shortcut: Combine the two ratios into A:B:C first, then split the total.

questions.questionText: The ages of Charan and Divya are in the ratio 3:4, and the ages of Divya and Esha are in the ratio 5:6. If the sum of all three ages is 236 years, what is Esha's age?
questions.explanation: Make Divya's part equal: Charan:Divya:Esha = 15:20:24. Sum of parts = 59, so one part = 236/59 = 4. Esha = 24 x 4 = 96 years.
questions.shortcut: Combine the two ratios into A:B:C first, then split the total.
